subject: Access log preservation & handover playbook - Q&A
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@truvehealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@truvehealth.com
Date: 2027-03-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Access logs: retention window & export options

Hi Alex,

Quick follow-up from our SOC2 prep: can you confirm what access/audit log retention windows Redwood supports for hosted tenants? Two scopes we're trying to cover:

- Short-term operational access logs (7-90 days) for incident debugging
- Long-term audit archives (up to 7 years) for compliance requests

Specifically:
1) What export formats and delivery methods do you support for bulk handover (CSV/JSON/parquet, S3 presigned, SFTP)?
2) Can exports be scoped to tenant-id + time range and redacted for PII before export?
3) If we request deletion evidence later, what proof do you provide (signed statement, export manifest, chain-of-custody)?
4) Any known constraints by region (us/eu) or minimum notice/lead time for large extracts?

We may need a short playbook that we can hand to our audit team — simple checklist and timelines. Can you send over?

Thanks,

Ellen Park
Security Operations
Truve Health

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@truvehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-13T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access logs: retention window & export options

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: yes, we support both short-term operational logs and longer-term archived exports; export formats include gzipped JSON/CSV and Parquet, and delivery via customer-managed S3 (preferred), SFTP, or a one-time pre-signed S3 URL. A few details and constraints below.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Retention: hosted tenants default to 90 days of hot access logs; we offer configurable archival to 7 years for enterprise plans via Dedicated/Private or paid archive add-on.
- Exports: CSV, JSON (newline-delimited), and Parquet are available. Exports are gzipped and checksummed (sha256). Delivery: S3 (push to customer bucket with role-based write), presigned PUT URL, or SFTP over FTPS.
- Scoping & redaction: Exports can be filtered by tenant_id, time range, and endpoint. PII redaction is supported as a pre-export step for defined fields (email, IP) but requires a configuration review (policy + sample) and typically 3–5 business days.
- Deletion evidence: We provide an export manifest (file list, checksums, timestamps), audit trail showing deletion activity, and a signed statement from our security team on request (enterprise SLA). Chain-of-custody for legal audit can be produced for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Region: EU tenants' logs are stored in-region; exports crossing regions require customer approval and may need an export permit for regulated data.
- Lead time: Small extracts (<50GB) typically 1–2 business days; large exports (50GB–2TB) 3–7 business days; >2TB will need scheduling and a runbook (7+ business days).

Attachments: I attached our access_log_schema.csv and a short export playbook (redwood_access_export_playbook.pdf) with example commands for S3/SFTP and sample manifests.

Action items:
- Ellen: can you confirm the target retention (e.g., keep 3yr archive) and preferred delivery method? If you need PII redaction, send sample fields to redact.
- Laura/Naomi: can you confirm capacity for a potential 500GB one-off export next month and the standard manifest template?

On technicalities:
- Exports are generated from immutable snapshots; each file has a sha256 checksum. Our service will keep a signed manifest and timestamps in our audit index for 12 months for hosted plans; for longer retention of manifests we recommend Dedicated/Private or a records export add-on.
- For deletion proofs we record who initiated deletion, job IDs, and a hash of exported files; we can produce signed manifests and evidence packages on request under enterprise agreements.

If useful, I can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with engineering to go over the playbook and S3 permissions.

Best,

Alex Martinez
Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@truvehealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access logs: retention window & export options

Alex — adding a couple of compliance notes and a brief suggested playbook below that we can send to Ellen's audit team.

Compliance notes:
- For EU accounts we do not export logs outside EU without explicit customer approval; we flag exports for DPA review.
- PII redaction is treated as a transformation job; we keep an internal job id and audit trail of the transformation parameters (schema of removed fields) — that helps with later evidence requests.
- Costing: exports during business hours are included up to 500GB per year for enterprise; beyond that, we bill per-GB for processing and egress. Naomi, confirm numbers for the quote.

Suggested minimal playbook (copyable):
1) Customer requests extract via Support portal: include tenant_id, time range, desired format, and delivery method.
2) Redwood assigns an export job id and provides ETA (based on size tiers).
3) For PII redaction, customer provides field list and acceptance sample; redaction job scheduled (3–5 business days).
4) Export generated as gzipped files + manifest (sha256). Manifest signed by platform key.
5) Delivery: push to customer S3 with role-based write or provide presigned PUT URLs.
6) Customer confirms receipt; Redwood retains export job metadata for 12 months (longer for Dedicated/Private).
7) For deletion evidence: customer requests deletion certificate; Redwood provides manifest + deletion audit showing job id, operator ID, and timestamp.

I'll draft a short emailable playbook PDF and drop it in the Drive link Alex will share.

-Laura

Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference
